newsitem.title: USA: U.S. senator declines to endorse FCC commissioner.
newsitem.headline: U.S. senator declines to endorse FCC commissioner.

text.p: The head of the Senate Commerce Committee declined to endorse any move to renominate Rachelle Chong to the Federal Communications Commission.

Chong's term as a commissioner expires this summer and there has been speculation President Clinton could renominate her to fill one of two Republican seats that would be vacant on the five-member FCC.
"Serious consideration should be given to another commissioner," Sen John McCain, an Arizona Republican, told a news conference. He declined to offer details.

McCain also repeated an endorsement for Justice Department attorney Michael Powell to fill a Republican seat at the FCC. Powell, chief of staff of the department's antitrust division, is son of retired Gen. Colin Powell.

McCain stressed, however, that a Powell nomination is not a "done deal." President Clinton has yet to name a new nominee after a top FCC official, Regina Keeney, took herself out of consideration late last year because of family concerns.
Meanwhile, McCain repeated his strong support for spectrum auctions.

Citing Clinton's call for $36.1 billion in new spectrum auctions in the fiscal 1998 budget proposal, McCain said the political landscape has changed for TV broadcasters, who have strongly opposed having to buy the rights for digital TV brodcasts.
"This will set off a series of negotiations and hearings on this issue," said McCain.
